correctness.rationale: On P=(P1)^m with smooth ample F(2,...,2) and X=F∩G(d_i>=3), dim X=m−2>=4, two integral weak Lefschetz applications give H²(P,Z)≈H²(X,Z) and inject H4(P,Z)→H4(X,Z). Hodge and exponential sequence identify Pic(X)=Z⟨H_i⟩. The squares of divisors D=sum a_i H_i vanish exactly when all mixed a_i a_j=0, so primitive square-zero Pic classes are ±H_i; nefness rules out minus. Every automorphism permutes H_i. Koszul/Kunneth twisted by e_i gives H0(X,H_i)=H0(P,O(e_i))=C², producing a unique ambient product automorphism (projections of X are onto P1). Adjunction K_X=sum d_i H_i restricts permutations to equal d_i. Koszul twisted (2,..,2) proves h0(I_X(2,..,2))=1, so the extension preserves F. Independent integer cohomology Kunneth checks of twisted bundles passed for nonuniform m=6,8 tuples. This confirms boundary vanishings but does not certify Lefschetz or prove the infinite result by enumeration.
residual_risks: Hypotheses smoothness/codimension essential; finite cohomology tests not universal proof

originality.rationale: Direct full comparison with Quedo shows the formerly proved smooth Wehler case is scalar uniform degree, deliberately excluded here. Primitive nonuniform canonical polarization (e.g. (3,3,3,3,3,4)) falls outside the cited scalar-power criterion, and intrinsic square-zero recovery provides a new all-smooth-sections argument. An uninspected broad multiprojective theorem is the main residual risk.
